name: Pastel Red
lede: Pastel Red names a softened, paled-down [[red]] by plain modifier grammar, and the xkcd 2010 crowd survey is the only dated record our sources carry for it.

sections.title: A modifier, surveyed in 2010
sections.body:
The name follows the modifier pattern "pastel" plus the parent hue [[red]], meaning a lightened, less saturated version of it [1]. Our library's only dated record for this exact pairing is the 2010 xkcd online color-naming survey, where visitors typed words next to swatches [2]. Paterson's dictionary separately defines a *pastel red* in the general sense, as a term applied to any softened red such as "fondant pink" [3], but ties no single coinage to this swatch.

The nearest named colors by measured distance are [[indian-red]], duller, and [[dark-coral]], almost the same shade [4]. [[strawberry-pink]] is duller still; [[coral-red]] reads almost the same, and [[cedar-chest]] and [[light-jasper-red]] sit further out, both duller [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings finds a match for this red in 46 of them, about 0.19 percent, rarer than 52 percent of the named colors we track, as photographed [5]. It peaks in the 1900s, at 1.7 times the expected rate for that century (6 of 1,674 paintings from then), and inside a painting it plays an accent in 76 percent of cases, ranked by lightness rather than raw area, so varnish cannot fake the result [5]. It is most over-represented in Indian paintings, at 3.4 times the expected rate [5]. The earliest match is dated 1320, long before the name's own 2010 record; the archive's early centuries are thin, so that date is a floor, not a first, and a resemblance in an aged photograph is not proof that any pigment or name existed then [5].
